mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate over the past month compresses the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines over the prior month, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 6.5% for two consecutive months, it signals a weakening labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts and retail sales signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate revenue expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS rise consecutively for two months, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle where the federal funds rate exceeds 0.5%, the central bank's policy stance reduces liquidity and increases borrowing costs, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly expansion in real GDP growth, measured by the annualized GDP series, indicates a strengthening economy that supports corporate earnings and generates positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of quarters when GDPC1 growth is positive, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year CPI inflation rate exceeds 2.5%, it triggers central bank tightening expectations that depress equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 2.5%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: When manufacturing output (INDPRO) and non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) both rise simultaneously, it indicates a synchronized expansion in production and labor markets that boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when both INDPRO and PAYEMS rise consecutively for two months, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: In a high unemployment regime where the unemployment rate exceeds 6.0%, a labor market recovery is underway, which increases consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 6.0%, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.02.
